chunks: And by this chain, it was said, it was said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)
He who exposes himself to suspicion, let him not blame the one who thinks ill of him; and he who conceals his secret, the choice is in his hand.

key_terms.أَسَاءَ بِهِ الظَّنَّ: thought ill of him / had bad opinion

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic teaching on exposing oneself to suspicion and keeping secrets?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ali (AS) in Al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the principle of 'zill al-zalalah' (casting suspicion) as a natural consequence of one's own actions, emphasizing personal accountability in social dynamics. It further highlights the virtue of 'kashf al-sirr' (concealment of secrets) as a means of preserving dignity and autonomy, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on modesty and prudence.
